solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hit hard, hospital in wreck

blocks.note: to trash something is to wreck it
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone struck hard and taken to hospital after a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts you to read 'hospital in wreck' as a news report; it is really instructions for putting H into TRASH.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word means to beat someone repeatedly and violently.

clue.text: Lucky thing beginning to train wild animals

blocks.note: first letter of train
anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A circus trainer lucky enough to be starting work with wild beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucky thing' looks like an exclamation about the trainer, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring good luck.

clue.text: Enjoy embracing local issue again

blocks.note: to relish something is to enjoy it
a local is the pub nearest your home

explanation.surface: Someone happily hugging the local paper as it comes out once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for your nearby pub, not a local newspaper as the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: RE- means again, and to publish is to issue a book or paper.

clue.text: Mug punched by head of police, intervene

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
something punched by a fist has it driven inside

blocks.note: a stein is a large beer mug
first letter of police

explanation.surface: A victim thumped by a senior officer, and a call for someone to come between them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' reads as a person being hit, but it is the drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: stepping into a dispute, like a referee, is intervening.

clue.text: Hit hard, drunk

blocks.note: struck repeatedly, as a carpenter's tool does to a nail
a slang sense: very intoxicated

explanation.walkthrough: This shares its first definition with 1 across, a little game by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammered means struck hard, and is also slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Plant leaf Victorian, withered

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

explanation.surface: An old plant specimen from the Victorian era, its leaf dried up.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder runs exactly the answer's thirteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The African violet is a popular flowering houseplant.

clue.text: Trough containing a head

blocks.note: a manger is a feeding trough for animals
used as printed

explanation.surface: A feeding trough with a head in it, perhaps of a hungry animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' sounds like part of a body in the trough, but it means a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the head of a team, shop or department is the person who runs it.

clue.text: Indian dish, almost a crown, served up

indicators.note: almost all of TIARA means it stops one letter short
in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom

blocks.note: used as printed
TIARA, a jewelled crown, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A curry dish arriving with an almost regal presentation.
explanation.walkthrough: A and TIAR join as ATIAR, and that whole string turns upward to read RAITA.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is an Indian side dish of yoghurt with cucumber or herbs.

clue.text: Level rising higher, house ends in river

blocks.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland
last letters of rising, higher and house

explanation.surface: Floodwater rising higher until the house stands in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like a reversal indicator in a down clue, but it only lends its final G.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a level or extent, as in 'to some degree'.

clue.text: By the sound of it, circuits failing

indicators.note: we are told to go by how the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: laps are circuits of a track

explanation.surface: Someone noticing electrical circuits breaking down from the noise they make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circuits failing' reads as electrics; the circuits are laps of a track.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a failing, a slip in standards or memory.

clue.text: Being a mum say, evidently exhausted with respect to feeds

blocks.note: someone exhausted is panting for breath
re means with respect to, as in memo headers

explanation.surface: A worn-out new mother, plainly shattered by all the night feeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeds' looks like part of the baby picture, but it is the instruction to put RE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Parenting is the job of being a mother or father; 'say' marks a mum as one example.

clue.text: Treasured bits in octets?

blocks.note: read one way, coins in a pirate's chest
read the other way, the parts that make up a group of 8

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the bits in an octet are pieces of a group of eight; the question mark flags the pun, and 'treasured' points to pirate gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Pieces of eight were old Spanish silver coins, the classic pirate treasure.

clue.text: Retired American Lord not entirely noble

indicators.note: not all of BLIMEY is used; its last letter goes

blocks.note: US is short for American
'Lord!' and 'Blimey!' are both exclamations of surprise; BLIMEY loses its Y

explanation.surface: A retired American peer who is not quite fully aristocratic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lord' seems to be a title, but it is the exclamation, as in 'Lord!', which is 'Blimey!' in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means lofty or noble in character.

clue.text: Correct once tag connected

indicators.note: to correct letters is to set them right, rearranging them

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters

explanation.surface: A label that was once right, now attached to something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Correct' at the front reads as an adjective, but it is a verb telling you to fix the order of ONCE TAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related or connected, especially of words sharing an origin.

clue.text: Central Line, a number westbound

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left

blocks.note: used as printed
six is a number

explanation.surface: A London Underground announcement about a westbound Central line train.
explanation.walkthrough: The Central line is a London Tube line, and 'westbound' fits the Tube picture; here the definition is a line through the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is a central line about which something turns or is symmetrical.

clue.text: Bacon endlessly inspiring one new artist

indicators.note: LARDON without its end loses the final N

blocks.note: a lardon is a small strip of bacon; endlessly, LARDO
anagram fodder, 3 letters

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon, the painter, tirelessly inspiring a new young artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Bacon looks like the painter Francis Bacon, which suits 'artist', but it is the food.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: da Vinci, the Italian Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, is an artist.

clue.text: If not white, rose hybridised

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A gardener breeding roses, happy to get any colour but white.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'white' from 'rose' to hide the phrase WHITE ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means if not, as in 'hurry, otherwise we'll miss it'.

clue.text: Promise to wrap the box? It’s a given!

blocks.note: an IOU is a written promise to pay
the box and the telly are British slang for the television

explanation.surface: A pledge to gift-wrap a box, with the cheery insistence that it is a present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A given' reads as a gift in the surface, but it means something certain.
explanation.definitionFit: 'I tell you!' is said to insist that something is certain, a given.

clue.text: Significant this novel, or one chapter

indicators.note: a novel form is a new one

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
used as printed
I is the Roman numeral one
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A reader deciding whether the whole novel is important or only one chapter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book, which suits 'chapter', but it is an adjective telling you to rework THIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means significant, important enough to be remembered.

clue.text: Offence including fray, prepare to deliver evidence

blocks.note: a sin is an offence
to fray is to wear, as cloth wears thin

explanation.surface: A charge that includes a brawl, with a witness getting ready for court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fray' suggests a fight to go with 'offence', but here it is the verb for wearing thin.
explanation.definitionFit: A witness is sworn in, taking the oath, before giving evidence.

clue.text: Photograph completely gone

blocks.note: a picture taken with a camera, as in 'a good one of the bride'
an informal sense: worn out or ruined, as frayed nerves are

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings sit side by side with no link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is a photograph, and something shot is ruined or worn out.

clue.text: Many stores, we hear?

indicators.note: what we hear is the sound of a word, not its spelling

blocks.note: hoards are stores, hidden stocks of something

explanation.surface: A remark that there are plenty of shops, as far as we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stores' looks like shops, but it means stockpiles, hoards.
explanation.definitionFit: Hordes are great crowds, many people or things.

clue.text: Out to make good a perfect place

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 3 letters
PI is short for pious, a crossword stand-in for good
used as printed

explanation.surface: Someone setting out to make a place good, even perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make good' reads as a phrase meaning repair; split it, and 'good' alone is PI.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Thomas More's 1516 book about an ideal island state.

clue.text: Offensive view attributed to leaders of our brotherhood

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

blocks.note: first letters of our and brotherhood
a scene is a view

explanation.surface: An objectionable opinion blamed on the heads of a fraternity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive view' reads as one phrase, a nasty opinion; the definition is only 'Offensive'.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means offensive to accepted standards of decency.

clue.text: Channel showing every western ever recorded, initially

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each word

blocks.note: first letters of showing, every, western, ever, recorded

explanation.surface: A TV channel that screens every cowboy film ever made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' fits the TV surface, but it is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewer is a channel carrying away waste water.

clue.text: Misprint 51 later corrected

indicators.note: to correct is to set right

blocks.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
anagram fodder, 5 letters

explanation.surface: A printing error on page 51 that was fixed afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all about a misprint being fixed, which is what makes it neat.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing, a literal is a typing error of a letter or two.

clue.text: Not up left? Absolutely!

blocks.note: the opposite of up is down
the 'Not' also applies here: not left is right

explanation.surface: An eager reply confirming that someone is not up and to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' does double duty, negating both 'up' and 'left'.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright means utterly, as in 'downright rude', much like absolutely.

clue.text: Aware of somewhere to go

blocks.note: an adjective, sharing knowledge of something secret
a coy phrase for a toilet, here an old outdoor one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere to go' is a coy way to say a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To be privy to something is to be aware of it; a privy is an outdoor toilet.

clue.text: Calm required, entire sherry emptied out!

indicators.note: an emptied word has lost its middle, leaving only its outer letters
the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters
outer letters of sherry

explanation.surface: Someone must stay calm, the whole sherry bottle having been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' and 'out' both look like signs of a drained bottle; one takes the outside of SHERRY, the other mixes the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a peaceful, untroubled state.

clue.text: Something to get through, a posh cake

blocks.note: you get through a gate
used as printed
U means upper-class, posh, in British usage

explanation.surface: A fancy cake that takes some effort to eat all of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to get through' suggests a big cake to finish; it is really a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, borrowed from French: a rich layered cake, often with cream.
